text: {"headline":"Elevated 99215 use runs above expectation at every complexity level, including low-complexity patients, but records are too thin to tell upcoding from a sicker panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The 99215 excess is not confined to complex patients. The share exceeds the all-provider rate in every condition band, and about a quarter of 99215s fall on patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions. Sampled examples include visits with simple diagnoses, such as C0059105 (J06.9 only), C0059638 (N39.0 only) and C0059253 (R21 only), which is a pattern consistent with upcoding. Against that, the high-complexity samples (e.g., C0059423, C0059911) look appropriate for 99215. The documentation that exists supports the billed levels: no documented claims fell below the billed level, and the three documented 99215s, including the low-complexity C0059809, recorded high MDM. No data-reviewed red flags appeared. Three documented 99215s is far too few to judge support, so a reviewer should first request charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed in the packet and check whether the MDM and time actually documented justify the highest level."}
